title: Elabora course (course.json)
description: Root file of an Elabora course project. It lists the sections and the order of screens, declares variables, the theme, navigation, completion and tracking rules. Screens live in screens/<id>.json, the validated plan in plan.json.

format.description: Format identifier and version. Always "elabora/0.1" for this version of the specification. Older courses are migrated by elabora migrate (Elabora reads them migrated in memory meanwhile).

id.description: Stable course identifier. Used for the SCORM manifest identifiers: changing it makes LMSs treat the package as a different course.

title.description: Course title shown to learners and in the LMS.

description.description: Short description for the LMS catalogue.

language.description: Language of the content. Selects the player labels (fr and en are built in).

version.description: Content version of the course. Increase it at every delivery.

durationMinutes.description: Typical learner duration, written into the SCORM manifest metadata.

sections.description: Ordered sections (modules) of the course. Each lists the ids of its screens, in learner order. Every screen must appear exactly once.

variables.description: Course variables, readable and writable by events. Persisted variables are saved in the learner's suspend data, so their size counts against the LMS budget.

speakers.description: The voices and characters of the course (narration lines and dialogue lines name them): the name shown in captions, the transcript and dialogue bubbles, the voice that speaks each language, and in dialogues their colour and look.

narration.description: Defaults of the course's narrated screens (each screen's narration may say otherwise).

seek.description: How far learners may move in their timeline (screen narration.seek): seen, back anywhere and forward up to the furthest point reached; free, anywhere. Whether the seek bar shows at all is the player's (player controls option seekBar); a screen may still hide its own (screen narration.seek none).

player.description: The learner's player around the screens (docs/decisions.md D58): two bars, top and bottom, each an ordered list of items. An item shows when it is enabled and has something to show (resources, glossary, credits and the logo need their content; exit shows in SCORM packages only); a bar with nothing to show is removed and the screen takes its room. A bar left out (or without its own items) takes its default items, less those placed in the other bar; an item left out of both bars is not shown. Each item may be in one bar only (the spacer once in each bar). Its colours and size come from the theme's player.* tokens.

top.description: The bar above the screen. Default: logo (disabled), title, progress, spacer, resources, glossary, credits, exit.

bottom.description: The bar below the screen. Default: outline, controls, spacer, previous, next.

resources.description: What learners may open or download from the player's Resources: files of assets/ shipped in the package (a job aid, a checklist, a form), and links (a page of the intranet). A PDF or an image opens in a preview over the module with « Télécharger »; any other file downloads; a link opens in a new tab. Shown by the player item resources.

title.description: What learners read in the list (« Fiche réflexe : incident réseau »).

description.description: One line on what the file is for, under its title.

asset.description: The file, relative to assets/ (resources/fiche-reflexe.pdf). PDF, office documents, text, images, audio, video or ZIP: formats every LMS web server serves (W_RESOURCE_TYPE otherwise). A resource has an asset or a url.

url.description: A link instead of a file, opened in a new tab: an https:// address (E_RESOURCE_URL otherwise).

glossary.description: The course's glossary: the terms learners may look up from the player's Glossary (a panel with search, entries in alphabetical order). A text links a word to its entry with a Markdown link to glossary:<id> ([passerelle](glossary:gateway)): the player shows the definition when it is hovered or focused, and the link opens the Glossary there. Translated with the course.

definition.description: One to three sentences, plain text.

translate.description: false: « Le terme ne se traduit pas »: the term and its variants are not sent for translation and stay as they are in every language (a product name, a procedure code); the definition still is translated.

variants.description: Other forms and synonyms learners may search for (plural, acronym, spelled out): « VPN », « réseau privé virtuel ».

source.description: Where the term was found when it was gathered (« Relever les termes »): a source of the author's sources/ (D49) or a screen of the course. For the author and the editor, which shows it beside the entry: never shown to learners, never translated, left out of packages.

kind.description: source: a file of sources/; screen: a screen of the course.

id.description: The source's name in sources/ (« brief-client.pdf »), or the screen's id.

at.description: Where in it, as the author would find it: « p. 4 », « diapositive 12 », « 02:15 ».

credits.description: The author's credits, one line each (« Conception pédagogique : Claire Martin », « Photographies : … https://… »): shown in the player's « IA et crédits » after what the course says by itself (its AI-generated voices and media, its voices' attributions). Addresses become links. Translated with the course.

sounds.description: The course's sounds (docs/decisions.md D67). Sound files live in assets/sounds/ (<id>.<ext>, with their sidecar <id>.json saying where the sound comes from and its licence) and are named by their id.

interface.description: Interface sounds: short sounds the player makes after a learner's gesture (a choice, a feedback good, fair or bad, going back or replaying, opening and closing the history or the debrief, a dialogue's successful end), the same in dialogues and questions. Learners switch them off in « Affichage » (« Sons de l'interface »); the player's volume applies.

when.description: auto: on when the module has sound (a narration, a dialogue's voices, an audio or video block, a sound of the story, music or an ambience), off otherwise: a silent module does not start clicking; on: always; off: never.

volume.description: Their volume, under the player's own (1: the files' level).

replace.description: A role's sound replaced by a sound of the course (its id in assets/sounds/), or null: that role makes no sound.

select.description: Choosing an option of a dialogue.

good.description: A good choice, a correct answer.

bad.description: A choice to avoid, a wrong answer.

back.description: Going back to a choice, starting over, replaying.

open.description: Opening a dialogue's history or debrief.

pronunciations.description: How generated voices say words of the whole course (an acronym, a reference, a name), by language: each language has its own list, never translated.

ignored.description: Warnings the author looked at and chose to ignore (docs/decisions.md D31): the validator marks the finding of that code with that key ignored, and it counts no more. A key names what the finding is about and a fingerprint of what was found (a swallowed word: the line, the word and its take's audio), so a finding that changes (another take) comes back. Written by the editor (ignore_findings), not by update_course; unlike plan waivers, nobody approves them, and the proof dossier says them ignored by the author. Never shipped in packages.

code.description: The code of the finding ignored: a warning or an information, never an error.

key.description: The finding's key (Diagnostic.key): what it is about, then @ and the fingerprint of what was found.

presentation.description: How screens are presented. scroll: a document per screen (default); steps appear one below the other. slides: every screen is one view that should fit the window (checked by elabora fit and elabora test at the fit sizes); steps appear in their reserved place. Sizes are in px at the reference window (1600×900) and follow the size classes of the player (1rem is 14 px at 1280×720).

contentWidth.description: Width of the reading column (blocks of width full), in px at the reference window; emitted in rem, so it follows the size classes.

wideWidth.description: Width of wide blocks and of the screen, in px at the reference window; emitted in rem.

fit.description: Window sizes (width x height, CSS px, inside the LMS frame) where a slide must fit without scrolling. reference: the size the course is designed for; an overflow there is a warning (W_SLIDE_OVERFLOW). minimum: the smallest supported size; slides may scroll there and an overflow is only reported (I_SLIDE_OVERFLOW_MINIMUM). Below it, and on phones, slides read as a scrolling page.

navigation.description: Player navigation rules: where learners may go. What the player shows (the outline, the progress, Previous and Next) is course.json player (D58).

mode.description: linear: learners go on with Next, and the outline opens the screens already reached. free: learners can also jump to any screen from the outline.

lockUntilComplete.description: If true, Next refuses to go on (a tooltip says why) until the current screen is complete.

completion.description: How the course reports completion and success to the LMS. The final status is sent once, when it is decided (never only at exit).

reportAs.description: Status pair reported in SCORM 1.2 cmi.core.lesson_status, as in Storyline. completed-incomplete: completed when all required screens are complete. passed-incomplete: passed when required screens are complete and the score reaches masteryScore. passed-failed: passed or failed once every scored item is answered. completed-failed: completed when required screens are complete, failed if the score is below masteryScore.

masteryScore.description: Passing score in percent. Required for every reportAs except completed-incomplete. Written to the manifest as adlcp:masteryscore.

exitAfterCompletion.description: Value of cmi.core.exit once the course is complete. suspend keeps resume data for review; normal ends the attempt. Never logout (SuccessFactors logs the learner out).

recordInteractions.description: Write quiz, decision and free-object answers to cmi.interactions, linked to plan objectives.

heartbeatSeconds.description: Periodic commit of session time while the course is open (0 disables). Keeps long sessions alive in LMSs that expire them.

delivery.description: How the SCORM package is delivered.

mediaQuality.description: Preset of the video, audio and raster images shipped in the package (elabora build --media-quality overrides it for one build). high: the masters the project keeps (video H.264 long side ≤ 1920, CRF 21, ≤ 8 Mb/s, AAC 160 kb/s; audio AAC 160 kb/s; images long side ≤ 3200, WebP q 88). medium: renditions encoded from the masters (video ≤ 1280, CRF 24, ≤ 4 Mb/s, AAC 128 kb/s; audio AAC 128 kb/s; images ≤ 2400, q 80). low: smaller renditions for LMSs with tight size limits (video ≤ 854, CRF 27, ≤ 1.5 Mb/s, ≤ 30 fps, AAC 96 kb/s; audio AAC 96 kb/s; images ≤ 1600, q 72). A rendition that would be larger than its master ships the master; SVG images are never re-encoded. E_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE says what the lower presets would weigh.

lms.description: The LMS the course is delivered to: ids of LMS profiles (elabora profiles lists them). elabora build, validate and test target them when no --profile is given: the package must fit their limits (size, files, suspend data). Without it the course targets an unknown LMS: the strictest documented behaviour, and package limits only warn, naming the LMSs that would refuse the package.

ui.description: Overrides for player labels, keyed by label id (see docs). Example: {"next": "Continuer"}.

translationOf.description: Set by elabora translate build: this course is the translation of another (its id, version and language). Generated: edit the source course and its translations/<lang>.xlf.

items.description: The items of the bar, in order from the start of the line (left in left-to-right languages). With a spacer, what is before it goes to the start of the line and what is after it to the end. Without one, the room left goes to the title or the controls, else before the first of resources, glossary, language, display, credits, exit, previous and next that follows another item.

position.description: window: the bar stays in the window (at its top or its bottom) while the page scrolls. page: the top bar scrolls away with the page; the bottom bar comes at the end of the page, after its content and once its last step is shown, like the end of a lesson in Rise (scroll presentation; the controls of a narrated screen stay in the window). In slides the page ends with the window: both look alike.

id.description: logo: the course's logo image. title: the course title. progress: the share of required screens completed. spacer: « Espace flexible », what is before it goes to the start of the line and what is after it to the end (the controls stretch first, the spacer takes what remains); one in each bar, always on. outline: the drop-down table of contents (sections and screens, what is done, what is not open yet). controls: the controls of narrated screens (play, replay, seek bar, time, captions, settings, volume, transcript). resources: the course's resources. glossary: the course's glossary. language: « Langue », the languages the package holds, to switch in place (shown when it holds more than one: elabora build --languages all). display: « Affichage », the learner's text size, larger captions and the keyboard shortcuts. credits: « IA et crédits », what was made with AI and the credits. previous, next: the navigation buttons; unavailable, they stay in place, greyed. exit: « Quitter », saves and ends the session (D3; SCORM packages only).

enabled.description: false: the item stays in the list (and its options) but is not shown. The spacer is always on.

options.description: The options of the item (see allOf below): logo { asset, alt, plate }, outline { screenTitle }, controls { seekBar, captionsByDefault, volume, transcript, speeds }, glossary { linkTerms }.

asset.description: The logo, relative to assets/ (SVG, PNG, WebP or JPEG; any size): the player scales it to the height of the bar.

alt.description: What the logo says (an organisation's name). Leave it out when the title next to it says it: the logo is then decorative.

plate.description: The logo on a light plate: for a dark logo on a dark bar (W_PLAYER_LOGO_CONTRAST says when an SVG logo would not read on its bar).

screenTitle.description: The button reads the title of the screen shown instead of « Sommaire ».

seekBar.description: Show the seek bar (how far it goes: course narration.seek). false: Play, Pause, Replay, the time and the step in words.

captionsByDefault.description: Captions are on when a learner first comes (each learner's own choice is kept afterwards).

volume.description: Show the volume (mute, and a slider).

transcript.description: Show the transcript button (the script of the screen, by step, with its speakers).

speeds.description: The playback speeds learners may choose: none (1× only), 0.75× to 1.5×, or 0.75× to 2× (recommended: learners who go at their own pace stay).

linkTerms.description: « Relier les termes aux écrans »: Elabora links each term or variant the first time it is in each screen (glossary:<id> links in the texts) when the option is turned on, when a term is added and on demand (elabora player --link-terms), never on its own afterwards: a link the author removed stays removed.

id.description: Named by narration lines and dialogue lines (speaker), and by a dialogue's learner.

name.description: The name learners read in captions and in the transcript (Leïla, Narrator).

narrator.description: A narrator rather than a character: in a dialogue (D61) its lines are said with its voice and shown as narration, centred, without a bubble or a portrait.

color.description: The theme colour of this character's name and bubble in a dialogue (a token: color.accent, or a custom color.* token), contrast-checked like the theme's.

look.description: How the character is drawn in a dialogue (D61): an SVG that follows the characters' convention ({ "svg": "personnages/marc.svg" }: its root declares data-expressions, data-gestures and data-portrait, and the player animates its mouth, expressions and gestures), or pictures ({ "portrait": "personnages/marc.webp", "expressions": { "inquiet": "personnages/marc-inquiet.webp" } }). Expressions and gestures not declared here are warnings (W_DIALOGUE_LOOK). Without a look: the name and an initial.

svg.description: An SVG of assets/ that follows the characters' convention (docs/dialogues.md).

portrait.description: A picture of the character's face (the neutral expression).

expressions.description: Pictures by expression name: the closed list of the faces the character may show.

voices.description: The voice that speaks each language, keyed by language tag (fr, en, fr-CA): the voice tools generate the lines of this speaker with it, and a generated line made with another voice is out of date.

provider.description: The voice tool that makes it (a local model, a voice service).

voice.description: The provider's id of the voice.

name.description: The voice's name as its provider gives it, for a voice service whose voices Elabora does not list itself (ElevenLabs): shown to authors without asking the service. Information only: never makes a line out of date.

settings.description: What the provider needs besides the voice (speed, style…), as it defines it. ElevenLabs: model (eleven_v4 by default), stability and similarity (0 to 1).

variable.description: A course variable. Strings need maxLength so the suspend data budget can be computed.

default.description: Initial value; must match the type.

options.description: Allowed values of a choice variable.

persist.description: Save in suspend data so the value survives a relaunch.

theme.description: Visual identity. tokens: the client charter (checked for contrast). custom: extra named values (colours, sizes) exposed as CSS variables and to free objects. stylesheet: free CSS for the whole course (cascade layer elabora.theme; its top-level @layer overrides blocks: elabora.overrides). cascade: where the theme sits among the cascade layers. fonts: embedded font files. styles: named styles that authors can pick per block or screen. Text never lives here: it stays in blocks.

cascade.description: Order of the cascade layers (docs/decisions.md D32). components-over-theme (what elabora init writes): the player, the theme's rules (the course's defaults), the component stylesheets, then the theme's top-level @layer overrides { … } blocks (what it overrides in components on purpose). theme-over-components: the order before 13 October 2026, the theme after the components, which it overrides whatever the specificity; what a course without cascade gets, so that it keeps its look. elabora theme upgrade moves a course from the second to the first without changing its look.

color.primary.description: Main brand colour: buttons, progress, headings accents.

font.body.description: CSS font stack for text. Only system or embedded fonts: no external font URL.

player.top.background.description: The player's top bar (D58). Default: color.primary.

player.top.text.description: Text and icons of the top bar (contrast ≥ 4.5:1 with player.top.background). Default: color.onPrimary.

player.bottom.background.description: The player's bottom bar. Default: color.surface.

player.bottom.text.description: Text and icons of the bottom bar (contrast ≥ 4.5:1 with player.bottom.background). Default: color.primary when it has that contrast with color.surface, else color.text.

player.accent.description: Filled controls of the player: Next, Play, the seek bar, toggles turned on (contrast ≥ 3:1 with player.bottom.background). Default: color.primary.

player.onAccent.description: Text and icons on player.accent (contrast ≥ 4.5:1). Default: color.onPrimary.

player.progress.description: The filled part of the progress bar (contrast ≥ 3:1 with the bar it is in). Default: the text colour of that bar.

player.tooltip.background.description: The player's tooltips: refusals, hints, the seek bar's quote, glossary definitions. Default: color.text.

player.tooltip.text.description: Text of the tooltips (contrast ≥ 4.5:1 with player.tooltip.background). Default: color.surface.

player.radius.description: Corner radius of the player's buttons and panels in px; 999 (default) makes pills, as Lin draws them.

player.density.description: Size of the bars: comfortable (default: 56 and 72 px high at the reference window, 44 px buttons) or compact (48 and 60 px, for screens that need the room).

dialog.bubble.description: A character's bubble in a dialogue (D61). Default: color.text at 5 % on color.surface.

dialog.learner.description: The learner's bubble in a dialogue. Default: color.accent at 12 % on color.surface.

dialog.text.description: Text of the bubbles (contrast ≥ 4.5:1 with dialog.bubble and dialog.learner). Default: color.text.

dialog.wordSpoken.description: The words a voiced line has said, as its ink reveals them (contrast ≥ 4.5:1 with both bubbles). Default: dialog.text.

dialog.wordUnspoken.description: The words of a voiced line still to be said: a preview, faint (contrast ≥ 1.5:1 with both bubbles, and ≥ 3:1 with dialog.wordSpoken, for the ink to show). Default: dialog.wordSpoken at 38 % over the bubble.

dialog.note.description: The trainer's notes in a dialogue without a quality: their colour (contrast ≥ 3:1 with color.surface); a quality has its own (color.success, color.accent, color.error). Default: color.primary.

custom.description: Extra design tokens, for example {"color.blueprint": "#0F2A47", "space.section": "72px"}. Each becomes the CSS variable --t-<name with dots as hyphens> (--t-color-blueprint) in the player and in free objects, and can be bound to free-object props with x-token. Editors show them next to the charter tokens.

stylesheet.description: Free CSS for the course, in theme/ (cascade layer elabora.theme, after the player and the components). Style the documented DOM contract (docs/design.md): data-screen, data-layout, data-type, data-component, data-style, .t-* classes, --t-* variables. url() must point to files inside the course (theme/ for fonts and textures, assets/ for generated images); no @import, no external URL. Use var(--t-…) for colours so a charter change propagates.

fonts.description: Embedded fonts (WOFF2 or WOFF files in theme/). The player declares them with @font-face and passes them to free objects; reference the family in font.body / font.heading or in the stylesheet. Check the font licence allows embedding (OFL fonts do). A face split into subset files (latin, latin-ext) is one entry per file, each with its unicodeRange.

weight.description: Weight or weight range of a variable font, for example "100 900".

unicodeRange.description: The characters the file holds, as a CSS unicode-range, for example "U+0100-02BA,U+1E00-1E9F" (the latin-ext subset of a font): the browser downloads the file only for pages that use one of them. Default: every character.

styles.description: Named styles declared by the theme, per type (a built-in type, a course component id, or "screen"), with a one-line description for editors: {"callout": {"rule": "Key rule on a dark card"}}. Blocks and screens pick one with style; the player adds data-style and the class t-s-<name>; the stylesheet styles it. Styles declared for a type also apply to its forks. Components can declare their own styles in component.json. (Not to be confused with the callout prop variant: info, tip, warning, important.)

effects.description: Effects of the theme for timed blocks (block timing.in and timing.out effect), each with a one-line description for editors: {"pop": "Grows a little past its size, then settles"}. The stylesheet defines @keyframes t-fx-<name> (how the block comes) and may define @keyframes t-fx-<name>-out (how it goes; default: the first one played backwards). The player plays them at the timeline's time, as the built-in effects (none, fade, rise, slide, zoom, wipe, draw, whose names are taken). Keep them relative to the block (transform, opacity, clip-path, filter): never move the layout, never flash (WCAG 2.3.1).

backdrop.description: Decorative background behind every screen. Decoration only: it carries no information, takes no focus and is hidden from screen readers (a scene that teaches is a free-object block). layers: empty elements behind the course that the stylesheet paints and animates (.t-backdrop-layer[data-layer="far"]); the backdrop element carries data-screen, data-section, data-step, data-variant, data-screen-index, data-section-index, data-section-count and data-direction, and #elabora-app carries data-backdrop (the variant shown), so the stylesheet can react to where the learner is. object: a decorative free object (pedagogicalRole "decoration") mounted once behind the course for the whole session, given the same context. Under reduced motion CSS animations stop and the object shows still frames; on a slow machine the object freezes. Text over a backdrop must stay readable: elabora fit measures its contrast against the pixels behind it (W_TEXT_CONTRAST_MEASURED).

layers.description: Layer names, back to front: <div class="t-backdrop-layer" data-layer="<name>"> each.

object.description: Decorative free object of objects/<id>/ (pedagogicalRole decoration) and its prop values.

props.description: Prop values, checked against the manifest.

variants.description: Named variants a screen can pick with backdrop, each with a one-line description for editors: {"dim": "Darker sky behind dense screens"}. The stylesheet styles .t-backdrop[data-variant=…]; the object receives the variant.

default.description: The variant of the screens that pick none (a name of variants): a module dark throughout says it once. A screen still picks another variant, or none, with backdrop.
